chapterNote: The first psalm of Asaph, and a covenant lawsuit with God as prosecutor, judge, and plaintiff. Three names of God open it — El, Elohim, the LORD — and He summons the earth from sunrise to sunset, shines out of Zion with Sinai's fire and storm, and calls heaven and earth as the witnesses Moses once called, to judge His own people. Two defendants are arraigned. The first is the pious formalist whose altar is busy: God does not want the bulls and goats — every beast of the forest is His, the cattle on a thousand hills, and if He were hungry He would not tell us. He wants thanksgiving, kept vows, and to be called on in the day of trouble so that He can rescue and be glorified. The second is the hypocrite who recites the statutes with the covenant on his lips while running with thieves, sharing with adulterers, and slandering his own brother from an armchair; God's silence, he assumed, meant God was like him. It did not. The verdict is one sentence for both: consider this, you who forget God. And the last words are the psalm's whole positive case — thanksgiving glorifies Me, and to the one who sets his road in order I will show the salvation of God.

1.text: A psalm of Asaph. The Mighty One, God, the LORD, has spoken, and He summons the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting.
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] of ['for', Asaph, the KJV margin] Asaph [Asaph]. The mighty [El] God [Elohim], even the LORD [YHWH], has spoken [dabar], and called [qara] the earth [eretz] from the rising [mizrach] of the sun [shemesh] unto the going down thereof.
1.notes: El Elohim YHWH dibber (H410, H430, H3068, H1696): El, Elohim, YHWH — three names of God stacked, the only such opening in the Psalter, as in Joshua 22:22 — has spoken; va-yiqra-arets mi-mizrach-shemesh ad-meboo (H7121, H776, H4217, H8121): and SUMMONS the earth from sunrise to sunset — a court convened with the whole world as gallery. Asaph (H623) was David's chief musician (1 Chronicles 16:5); twelve psalms carry his name, and this is the first.

2.text: From Zion, beauty brought to perfection, God has blazed out in light.
2.amp: Out of Zion [Tsiyyon], the perfection of beauty [yophi], God [Elohim] has shined [yapha — shone forth].
2.notes: mi-Tsiyyon mikhlal-yophi Elohim hophia (H6726, H3308, H430, H3313): out of Zion, the completeness of beauty — Lamentations 2:15's phrase for the city, before it fell — God has SHONE FORTH: yapha, the theophany-verb of Deuteronomy 33:2, where He shone from Seir and Paran. Sinai's light now comes from Jerusalem's hill.

3.text: Our God comes and will not keep silent; before Him a fire devours, and around Him it storms mightily.
3.amp: Our God [Elohim] shall come [bo], and shall not keep silence [charash]: a fire [esh] shall devour [akal] before [panim] Him, and it shall be very [meod] tempestuous round about Him.
3.notes: yabo Elohenu ve-al-yecherash (H935, H430, H2790): our God COMES and will not be deaf-silent — charash, Psalm 28:1's dreaded silence, here refused; esh-le-phanav tokhel u-sebibav nisarah meod (H784, H6440, H398, H3966): fire eats before Him and around Him it storms exceedingly — Sinai's furniture (Exodus 19:16-18; Deuteronomy 4:11) brought to the courtroom. Hebrews 12:29's consuming fire.

4.text: He calls the heavens overhead and the earth as witnesses, so that He may judge His people:
4.amp: He shall call [qara] to the heavens [shamayim] from above, and to the earth [eretz], that He may judge [din] His people [am].
4.notes: yiqra el-ha-shamayim me-al ve-el-ha-arets (H7121, H8064, H776): He calls to the heavens above and to the earth — the two witnesses Moses summoned to the covenant (Deuteronomy 4:26; 30:19; 32:1), now recalled to testify — la-din ammo (H1777, H5971): to JUDGE His people. Not the nations: His own. The lawsuit is a covenant lawsuit, and the defendant is Israel.

5.text: 'Gather to Me My faithful ones, who cut a covenant with Me over sacrifice.'
5.amp: Gather [asaph] My saints [chasid — covenant-loyal ones] together unto Me; those that have made [karath — cut] a covenant [berith] with Me by sacrifice [zebach].
5.notes: isphu-li chasidai (H622, H2623): GATHER to Me My chasidim — a play many hear on the psalmist's own name, Asaph the gatherer — korete beriti ale-zabach (H3772, H1285, H2077): the cutters of My covenant over sacrifice — Exodus 24:5-8, the blood thrown on the altar and the people. God's first words in the psalm are a summons to the people who signed.

6.text: The heavens announce His righteousness, because God — He is the Judge. Selah.
6.amp: And the heavens [shamayim] shall declare [nagad] His righteousness [tsedek]: for God [Elohim] is judge [shaphat] Himself. Selah [Selah].
6.notes: va-yaggidu shamayim tsidqo (H5046, H8064, H6664): and the heavens DECLARE His righteousness — Psalm 19:1's heavens with a different subject, and Psalm 97:6's exact line; ki-Elohim shophet hu (H430, H8199): for God — He is Judge. Selah: the court is seated; the charges begin.

7.text: 'Hear, My people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against you: I am God, your God.'
7.amp: Hear [shama], O My people [am], and I will speak [dabar]; O Israel [Yisrael], and I will testify [ud — bear witness] against you: I am God [Elohim], even your God [Elohim].
7.notes: shimah ammi va-adabberah (H8085, H5971, H1696): HEAR, My people — the Shema's verb (Deuteronomy 6:4), and the Shema's God speaking — Yisrael ve-aidah bakh (H3478, H5749): Israel, and I will TESTIFY against you; Elohim Elohekha anokhi (H430): God, your God, am I — the first commandment's self-introduction (Exodus 20:2), now the prosecutor's. The covenant's Author files the complaint.

8.text: 'I am not reproving you for your sacrifices, and your burnt offerings are continually before Me.'
8.amp: I will not reprove [yakach] you for your sacrifices [zebach] or your burnt offerings [olah], to have been continually [tamid] before Me.
8.notes: lo al-zebachekha okhichekha (H2077, H3198): not for your sacrifices do I REPROVE you — ve-olotekha le-negdi tamid (H5930, H8548): and your whole-burnt-offerings are before Me continually. The charge is not neglect of the altar; the altar is busy. That is the surprise of the case: the defendants are the pious.

9.text: 'I will take no bull from your house, nor male goats from your pens.'
9.amp: I will take [laqach] no bullock out of your house [bayith], nor he goats out of your folds.
9.notes: lo-eqqach mi-betekha phar (H3947, H1004): I will not TAKE a bull from your house — mi-mikhleotekha attudim: nor goats from your pens. The animals were the required offerings (Leviticus 1:3; 4:23); God does not refuse them — He refuses the idea behind them, which verses 10-13 spell out.

10.text: 'For every creature of the forest belongs to Me, and so do the cattle on a thousand hills.'
10.amp: For every beast [chay] of the forest is Mine, and the cattle [behemah] upon a thousand [eleph] hills.
10.notes: ki-li khol-chayto-yaar (H2416): for MINE is every creature of the forest — behemot be-harere-aleph (H929, H505): the beasts on the hills of a thousand — 'a thousand hills', the English proverb this verse gave the language. Psalm 24:1's ownership claim applied to livestock: you cannot give God what is already His.

11.text: 'I know every bird of the mountains, and whatever moves in the field is Mine.'
11.amp: I know [yada] all the fowls of the mountains [har]: and the wild beasts of the field [sadeh] are Mine.
11.notes: yadati kol-oph harim (H3045, H2022): I KNOW every bird of the mountains — by name, as Matthew 10:29's sparrows — ve-ziz sadai immadi (H7704): and the moving things of the field are 'with Me', the margin's literal — in My keeping. The Creator's inventory (Psalm 104:24-27) as a rebuttal to the donors.

12.text: 'If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and everything that fills it are Mine.'
12.amp: If I were hungry, I would not tell [amar] you: for the world [tebel] is Mine, and the fulness [melo] thereof.
12.notes: im-erab lo-omar lakh (H7456, H559): IF I were hungry — the pagan premise, gods fed by their worshipers, stated to be mocked — I would not tell YOU; ki-li tebel u-meloah (H8398, H4393): for Mine is the world and its fullness, Psalm 24:1 quoted. Acts 17:25 preaches this verse at Athens: He is not served by human hands, as though He needed anything.

13.text: 'Do I dine on the flesh of bulls? Do I drink the blood of goats?'
13.amp: Will I eat [akal] the flesh [basar] of bulls [abbir — mighty ones], or drink [shatah] the blood [dam] of goats?
13.notes: ha-okhal besar abbirim (H398, H1320, H47): do I EAT the flesh of the mighty ones — abbirim, the strong bulls of Psalm 22:12 — ve-dam attudim eshteh (H1818, H8354): and drink the blood of goats? The rhetorical question that ends every sacrificial superstition: the altar was never God's dinner table (cf. Isaiah 1:11; Micah 6:6-8).

14.text: 'Sacrifice thanksgiving to God, and make good your vows to the Most High;
14.amp: Offer [zabach — sacrifice] unto God [Elohim] thanksgiving [todah]; and pay [shalam — make good] your vows [neder] unto the most High [Elyon]:
14.notes: zebach l-Elohim todah (H2076, H430, H8426): SACRIFICE to God thanksgiving — the todah, which was a real offering (Leviticus 7:12) and is here made the point of all the others — ve-shallem le-Elyon nedarekha (H7999, H5945, H5088): and pay the Most High your vows. What God wants from the altar is the heart's transaction: gratitude and kept promises (cf. Hebrews 13:15).

15.text: and call on Me in the day of trouble; I will rescue you, and you will glorify Me.'
15.amp: And call [qara] upon Me in the day [yom] of trouble [tsarah]: I will deliver [chalats — draw out] you, and you shall glorify [kabad] Me.
15.notes: u-qraeni be-yom tsarah (H7121, H3117, H6869): and CALL on Me in the day of trouble — achallesqekha u-tekhabbedeni (H2502, H3513): I will draw you out, and you will glorify Me. The third thing God asks for is to be asked: prayer as the sacrifice He actually wants, with the glory as His return. Spurgeon called the verse a check drawn on the bank of heaven; the psalm's whole positive case is verses 14-15.

16.text: But to the wicked God says: 'What business do you have reciting My statutes, or taking My covenant on your lips,
16.amp: But unto the wicked [rasha] God [Elohim] says [amar], What have you to do to declare [saphar — recite] My statutes [choq], or that you should take [nasa] My covenant [berith] in your mouth [peh]?
16.notes: ve-la-rasha amar Elohim (H7563, H559, H430): but to the WICKED God says — the second defendant: not the pagan but the insider who talks covenant; mah-lekha le-sapper chuqqai (H5608, H2706): what is it to you to RECITE My statutes — va-tissa beriti ale-phikha (H5375, H1285, H6310): and to lift My covenant on your mouth? Orthodox speech from an unorthodox life; Romans 2:17-24 is Paul's sermon on these verses.

17.text: since you hate discipline and throw My words behind you?
17.amp: Seeing you hate [sane] instruction [musar — discipline], and cast [shalak — fling] My words [dabar] behind [achar] you.
17.notes: ve-attah saneta musar (H8130, H4148): and YOU hate musar — discipline, correction, the word Proverbs opens with (Proverbs 1:2) — va-tashlekh debarai acharekha (H7993, H1697, H310): and you FLING My words behind you — the gesture of 1 Kings 14:9 and Nehemiah 9:26: the law over the shoulder like a rind.

18.text: When you saw a thief you were pleased to run with him, and you threw in your lot with adulterers.
18.amp: When you saw [raah] a thief [gannab], then you consented [ratsah — were pleased] with him, and have been partaker ['thy portion was with', cheleq, the KJV margin] with adulterers [naaph].
18.notes: im-raita gannab va-tirets immo (H7200, H1590, H7521): if you saw a thief, you were PLEASED with him — ratsah, delight, not mere tolerance — ve-im menaaphim chelqekha (H5003, H2506): and with adulterers 'your portion', the margin's literal — your share. The eighth and seventh commandments, in that order; the ninth comes next.

19.text: You let your mouth loose for evil, and your tongue harnesses deceit.
19.amp: You give ['sendest', shalach, the KJV margin] your mouth [peh] to evil [ra], and your tongue [lashon] frames deceit [mirmah].
19.notes: pikha shalachta be-raah (H6310, H7971, H7451): your mouth you SENT into evil, the margin's literal — let it off the leash. u-leshonekha tatsmid mirmah (H3956, H4820): and your tongue HARNESSES deceit — tsamad, to yoke, the word for Baal-peor's joining (Numbers 25:3): the tongue in the yoke and deceit pulling.

20.text: You sit and speak against your brother; you throw slander at your own mother's son.
20.amp: You sit [yashab] and speak [dabar] against your brother [ach]; you slander [natan — give out a slur against] your own mother's [em] son [ben].
20.notes: tesheb be-achikha tedabber (H3427, H251, H1696): you SIT — settled, at leisure — and speak against your brother; be-ben-immekha titten-dophi (H1121, H517, H5414): against your own mother's son you give a dophi, a slur — a word used only here. Slander as the sin of the comfortable: it is done sitting down.

21.text: These things you did, and I kept silent; you imagined that I was just like you. I will reprove you and lay the case out before your eyes.
21.amp: These things have you done [asah], and I kept silence [charash]; you thought [damah — imagined] that I was altogether [hayah] such an one as yourself: but I will reprove [yakach] you, and set them in order [arak — arrange the case] before your eyes [ayin].
21.notes: elleh asita ve-hecherashti (H6213, H2790): these you did and I was SILENT — charash, the silence verse 3 said He would break. dimmita heyot-ehyeh khamokha (H1819, H1961): you IMAGINED that I would be — 'I AM', the Exodus 3:14 verb hidden in the phrase — like you: the sinner's real theology is a god who shrugs at what he shrugs at. okhichakha ve-eerkhah le-enekha (H3198, H6186, H5869): I will reprove you and ARRANGE it before your eyes — arak, to set a case in order, item by item. The silence was patience, not agreement (cf. Romans 2:4; Ecclesiastes 8:11).

22.text: 'Consider this now, you who forget God, or I will tear you to pieces with no one to rescue:
22.amp: Now consider [bin — understand] this, you that forget [shakach] God [Eloah], lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver [natsal].
22.notes: binu-na zot shokheche Eloah (H995, H7911, H433): UNDERSTAND this now, forgetters of Eloah — the rare singular name, Job's word for God; pen-etroph ve-en matsil (H2963, H5337): lest I tear — the lion's verb, Hosea 5:14 — and there is no rescuer. Both defendants — the formalist (vv. 7-15) and the hypocrite (vv. 16-21) — share one diagnosis: they forgot God. Psalm 9:17's nations, now inside the covenant.

23.text: Whoever sacrifices thanksgiving glorifies Me, and to the one who sets his way in order I will show the salvation of God.'
23.amp: Whoso offers [zabach — sacrifices] praise [todah — thanksgiving] glorifies [kabad] Me: and to him that orders ['that disposeth his way', sum, the KJV margin] his conversation [derek — way] aright will I show [raah] the salvation [yesha] of God [Elohim].
23.notes: zobeach todah yekhabbedaneni (H2076, H8426, H3513): the sacrificer of todah GLORIFIES Me — verse 14's answer stated as the verdict; ve-sam derekh arennu be-yesha Elohim (H7760, H1870, H7200, H3468, H430): and the one who 'sets his way' — the margin's literal: puts his road in order — I will show him the salvation of God. Thanksgiving and an ordered walk: the two things the whole trial was about, and the last words are 'the salvation of God' — the phrase Luke 3:6 sets at the end of the prophet's road, and the thing Simeon said he had seen with the Child in his arms (Luke 2:30).
